blind_target.evidence_quote: Previous work has found that configuring participants into high-power versus low-power physical postures caused increases in subjective feelings of power, testosterone, and risk-taking as well as decreases in cortisol. We attempted to replicate and extend this pattern of findings by testing for the mediating role of testosterone and overconfidence in the relationship between power poses and risk-taking.
blind_target.outcome_quote: We were unable to replicate the findings of the original study and subsequently found no evidence for our extended hypotheses.
